documents.unit: Office of the VP for Academic Affairs, Academic Integrity
documents.title: FAQ: AI (Faculty)
documents.summary: A faculty FAQ from the academic integrity office. Its only AI-specific answer says that AI use not authorized for an assignment is reported as cheating; the rest explains how instructors report, meet students, and handle appeals for any integrity violation. The office does not say whether AI is allowed; authorization is left to the assignment.
documents.stance_why: The only AI answer says "If the use of artificial intelligence is not authorized for the assignment in question, the violation is 'cheating'". That sets no default allow or ban; whether AI is authorized is decided per assignment by the instructor, so the document delegates. Coder A coded delegates and coder B restrict; B read the 'not authorized' clause as a ban by default, but the FAQ never says AI is barred unless authorized, only how to label a violation once authorization is absent, so delegates is kept.

units.why: The answer ties AI to the existing integrity policy: "any form of unauthorized assistance constitutes cheating". This is a classification rule for misconduct (P36), not a stance on whether AI is allowed.
units.anchor: any form of "unauthorized assistance" constitutes cheating

units.why: When AI is "not authorized for the assignment in question" the violation is "cheating". This fixes what applies when authorization is missing (P06) and leaves authorization to each assignment; P36 is already used for the general classification above, and this unit adds the assignment-level default.
units.anchor: not authorized for the assignment in question, the violation is "cheating"
units.fit_note: It is written as the violation type instructors select, not as a rule for students. (Coder B: Stated as how to label a violation, not directly as a student rule.)

units.why: The threshold "a preponderance of evidence shows the student violated the policy" is a standard of proof for filing a report, hence P69.
units.anchor: A report should be filed if an instructor decides that a preponderance of evidence shows
units.fit_note: The standard is stated for all integrity violations, not AI specifically.

units.why: Instructors must use the form "for EACH violation". This is a reporting procedure after misuse is suspected, so P81.
units.anchor: Use the Academic Violation Report - Single Violation form for EACH violation

units.why: A single form may cover several violations "part of a single incident on a single date", otherwise separate reports. Procedural reporting rule (P81).
units.anchor: file one form for multiple violations so long as the violations were all part

units.why: "Cases must be reported to the Academic Integrity Office for each violation" is a duty to use the central reporting channel (P81), here justified by integrity being "intrinsic to education".
units.anchor: cases must be reported to the Academic Integrity Office for each violation

units.why: The reason given is that the university "has deemed academic integrity a value intrinsic to education and to the validity of a UNT degree". That grounds the rules in integrity and degree validity, not skill-building, so P95.
units.anchor: academic integrity a value intrinsic to education and to the validity of a UNT degree

units.why: "The faculty, administration, and students all have had input on the formulation" of the policy describes who made it (P84).
units.anchor: The faculty, administration, and students all have had input on the formulation
units.fit_note: It describes the student integrity policy 6.003, not an AI-specific policy. (Coder B: Concerns the general integrity policy, not an AI-specific one.)

units.why: "you need to meet with the student ... to give the student the opportunity to tell their side of the story" is a duty to talk with the student before filing, so P57. P64 (right to respond) is the student-side right, but this sentence is addressed to the instructor.
units.anchor: you need to meet with the student
units.frag_end: has been involved in an Academic Integrity violation.
units.policy: Before filing a violation form, the instructor meets with the student in person, by video, by phone, or possibly by email (least desirable) to give the student the opportunity to tell their side of the story.

units.why: Covers the case where the student does not respond: "If the student does not respond to you within 5 business days or declines, you may file the form". It is a step inside the meet-first rule, so it goes with that rule (P57) and not with the general filing procedure (P81).
units.anchor: If the student does not respond to you within 5 business days or declines
units.fit_note: Adds a fallback after 5 business days of no response, which P57 does not cover.
units.resolution_why: Coder A coded P81 (reporting procedure); coder B coded P57. The sentence follows 'you need to meet with the student' and says what the instructor does when the meeting does not happen, so a reader looking for the meeting rule would expect it under P57. Final P57 with B's fit note; actor, phase and modality (instructor, when-misuse, may) agreed.

units.why: Guidance to "file as soon as you identify the violation" sets a timing rule for reporting (P81).
units.anchor: Our guidance is to file as soon as you identify the violation

units.why: The office will not tell instructors the outcome or prior violations "under FERPA guidelines". No type covers confidentiality of case outcomes, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: the AI Office is not at liberty to disclose that information
units.uncovered_note: The integrity office does not tell the reporting instructor the sanctions, prior violations or appeal result, because of FERPA. (Coder B: about what the integrity office may not tell instructors (FERPA), not about what instructors must do; B coded it P81.)
units.fit_note: About what the integrity office may not tell instructors (FERPA), not about what instructors must do.
units.resolution_why: Coder A coded UNCOVERED, admin, must-not; coder B coded P81, instructor, informs. The passage says "the AI Office is not at liberty to disclose that information", so the party bound is the office (admin), and the rule is a confidentiality limit, not a reporting step the instructor follows. P81 (follow the formal reporting procedure) does not say that, so UNCOVERED is kept with both notes. Modality must-not because the office may not disclose.

units.why: "The student has the due process right to appeal each violation separately" gives accused students a right to contest, so P64.
units.anchor: The student has the due process right to appeal each violation separately
units.resolution_why: Coder A coded actor all; coder B coded student. The sentence states a right that belongs to the accused student ("The student has the due process right to appeal"), so the student is the actor. Type P64 and phase agreed.

units.why: Appeals "go to the chair of the department, who will gather information and make a ruling". This is the formal procedure after a sanction (P81).
units.anchor: The information will go to the chair of the department, who will gather information
units.frag_end: hear the appeal and issue a ruling.
units.resolution_why: Found only by coder A (B folded the appeal routing into its chair-discussion unit). "The information will go to the chair of the department, who will gather information and make a ruling" is a real appeal procedure; kept as its own unit because it states who rules, while the next unit states what instructors should avoid. P81, admin, informs.

units.why: Instructors "should avoid discussing the violation with your chair" until it is known whether there is an appeal, and are asked to contact the AI office. A procedural instruction (P81).
units.anchor: you should avoid discussing the violation with your chair
units.resolution_why: Coder B merged this sentence with the appeal routing into one should-not unit; coder A split them. The instruction to avoid discussing the case with the chair is its own rule, kept as a separate unit from the routing unit. Type, actor, phase and modality agreed.

units.why: Mentions a Canvas module "including instruction and a quiz on the UNT Academic Integrity Policy" and a full course; this offers integrity training materials for students, P70.
units.anchor: This module , including instruction and a quiz on the UNT Academic Integrity Policy, may
units.fit_note: Integrity training, not specifically AI literacy.
units.resolution_why: Found only by coder B. The source says the integrity module with instruction and a quiz "may be posted in Canvas classes for use in introductory classes", a permission for instructors to use integrity training. It is a real provision though not AI-specific; P70 is the nearest type, with B's fit note. Kept.

units.why: Directs instructors to "the Academic Integrity Decision Tree" that "will walk you through the academic integrity process"; a pointer to further guidance, P115.
units.anchor: Check out the Academic Integrity Decision Tree
units.resolution_why: Found only by coder B. "Check out the Academic Integrity Decision Tree! This decision tree will walk you through the academic integrity process" points instructors to further guidance on handling suspected violations, so it is a real pointer unit (P115). Kept.

documents.title: Artificial Intelligence guide: Faculty
tiers: Sample statements for teachers allowing AI with attribution
Sample statements for teachers prohibiting generative AI
documents.summary: A library guide for faculty that says every UNT syllabus should give clear AI guidance and that detection reports alone are not enough evidence. It then offers sample syllabus statements in three groups (all teachers, allow with attribution, prohibit) for instructors to adapt, adapted from UAB Libraries, and links to teaching readings.
documents.stance_why: The guide says "All course syllabi at UNT should include clear guidance as to permissible use of AI" and supplies statements for teachers who "allow" and who "choose to prohibit" AI. It sets no common rule and hands the choice to each teacher, offering three sets of templates, so it delegates with tiers.

units.why: "All course syllabi at UNT should include clear guidance as to permissible use of AI" asks every syllabus to state AI expectations (P09).
units.anchor: All course syllabi at UNT should include clear guidance as to permissible use of AI
units.resolution_why: Coder A coded phase course-start; coder B before-course. The sentence asks that every syllabus state AI expectations, which is communicating expectations to students, so course-start. Type P09, actor instructor and modality should agreed.

units.why: The reason given is the "inadequacy of detection tools" and the rapid change of AI, which states that detectors are unreliable (P39).
units.anchor: the inadequacy of detection tools
units.policy: AI technologies are rapidly evolving and detection tools are inadequate.
units.fit_note: The sentence about not relying on a detection report alone is coded separately as P69.
units.resolution_why: Both coders coded P39, actor all, when-misuse, informs. They worded the policy differently: coder A wrote 'detection results are not reliable', which goes beyond the source; coder B wrote 'Detection tools are inadequate.' Final wording follows the passage: 'the rapidly evolving nature of AI technologies and the inadequacy of detection tools'.

units.why: "A detection report alone (such as Turnitin) is not sufficient evidence for a violation" limits detector output to supporting evidence, which is the broadened P69.
units.anchor: a detection report alone (such as Turnitin) is not sufficient evidence for a violation

units.why: "Clear and concise course policies and explicit instructions ... are key to compliance" explains why instructors should spell out AI rules for assignments and assessments; it extends the syllabus-statement expectation (P09).
units.anchor: Clear and concise course policies and explicit instructions for course assignments
units.fit_note: It extends the syllabus duty to assignment and assessment instructions and states the compliance rationale.

units.why: The statements are "provided as examples for teachers", which supplies sample syllabus language (P110).
units.anchor: The following statements are provided as examples for teachers

units.why: Teachers are split into those who allow AI and those who "choose to prohibit its use"; the decision is left to the teacher, so P04.
units.anchor: for those teachers who choose to prohibit its use
units.policy: Teachers choose whether to allow generative AI with attribution or to prohibit its use.
units.resolution_why: Found only by coder A. The passage divides teachers into those who "will allow" AI with attribution and those who "choose to prohibit its use", so the choice is left to each teacher. It states the delegation, a real statement; P04 informs, instructor. Kept.

units.why: "Academic misconduct is present ... wherever AI assistance has been used when unauthorized" classifies unauthorized AI as misconduct (P36). The undisclosed-authorized half is coded as a separate unit.
units.anchor: wherever AI assistance has been used when unauthorized
units.policy: Academic misconduct is present in academic work wherever AI assistance has been used when unauthorized.
units.fit_note: Also makes failure to disclose authorized AI use a violation; that half is coded as a separate P28 unit.
units.resolution_why: Coder A split the sample sentence into two units, coder B kept one unit. The sentence has two distinct rules, so the split is kept. Coder A coded this half must-not, coder B informs. "Academic misconduct is present ... wherever AI assistance has been used when unauthorized" classifies behaviour as misconduct and does not itself command, so informs. Type P36, student, when-misuse agreed.

units.why: The same sentence says misconduct is present wherever authorized AI use "has not been disclosed as required", so failing to disclose is itself the violation (P28). It classifies, so informs, with unit_stance require because it makes disclosure mandatory.
units.anchor: when authorized, has not been disclosed as required
units.policy: Academic misconduct is present wherever authorized AI assistance has not been disclosed as required.
units.resolution_why: Found only by coder A (coder B kept both halves in one P36 unit and noted P28 in a fit note). The nondisclosure half is a separate rule and fits P28 exactly, so it is its own unit. Coder A coded must; changed to informs for the same reason as the unauthorized half: the sentence classifies.

units.why: "The rules that are expressed in this syllabus may need to change on short notice" says the policy is provisional (P54).
units.anchor: the rules that are expressed in this syllabus may need to change on short notice
units.resolution_why: Coder A coded over-time; coder B course-start. "The rules ... may need to change on short notice" says the policy is provisional and will be revised, which is review and revision (P54, over-time), though it appears in a syllabus statement. Type, actor and modality agreed.

units.why: "In principle you may submit material that contains AI-generated content ... if this use is properly documented" permits AI in writing by default and lists allowed uses (outline, sections, references). That is a permissive default (P02); the documentation duty is coded separately in the next unit.
units.anchor: you may submit material that contains AI-generated content, or is based on
units.policy: In principle students may submit material that contains AI-generated content, or is based on or derived from it, if this use is properly documented. This includes, for example, drafting an outline, preparing individual sections, combining elements, removing redundant parts, and compiling and annotating references.
units.fit_note: Applies to writing and requires documentation; the list of allowed uses is part of the passage.
units.resolution_why: Coder A coded P24 (disclose AI use); coder B coded P02 (permit by default). The passage mainly says AI-generated content may be submitted, with documentation as the condition, and lists permitted uses. A reader looking for 'AI is allowed in writing' would look under P02; the documentation requirement itself appears in the next sentence and is coded P24. Final P02. Actor, phase and modality (student, during-work, may) agreed.

units.why: "Your documentation must make the process transparent" requires documentation of AI use with the submission, together with "standards of attribution and validation". That is disclosure with each submission (P24).
units.anchor: Your documentation must make the process transparent
units.fit_note: It asks for process documentation, not a transcript or log.
units.resolution_why: Coder A coded P26 (keep and submit logs) with unit_stance require; coder B coded P24 with unit_stance permit. The passage requires documentation that makes the process transparent and meets 'standards of attribution', which is disclosure (P24); it does not name a transcript, log or reflection, so P26 fits less well. The student must document, so unit_stance require. P26 is used for the graded-documentation unit below.

units.why: "The use of AI tools is permitted, provided you follow our standards for attribution, validation, and transparency" is an open-book exam/quiz statement that allows AI. It permits, so P02; P22 (no AI on exams) says the opposite.
units.anchor: The use of AI tools is permitted, provided you follow our standards for attribution
units.fit_note: Applies only to an open-book exam or quiz, and the permission is conditioned on attribution, validation and transparency.
units.resolution_why: Coder A coded P24; coder B coded P02. The sentence's main act is permitting AI on an exam; the attribution condition is secondary. P02 is the permit-by-default type and B's note that P22 is the opposite supports it. Final P02. Actor, phase, modality (student, during-assessment, may) and unit_stance permit agreed.

units.why: "We encourage the use of such AI resources to inform yourself about the field ... and to help your learning" welcomes AI use, so P02 with unit_stance encourage.
units.anchor: We encourage the use of such AI resources to inform yourself about the field

units.why: "AI generated submissions cannot achieve a passing grade" bars AI-generated work from counting, so students may not have AI produce what they submit. P19 states that; the course's grading redesign is coded in the sample-solutions unit (P35).
units.anchor: AI generated submissions cannot achieve a passing grade
units.fit_note: Written as a grading consequence in a course that otherwise encourages AI use.
units.resolution_why: Coder A coded P19; coder B coded P35 (redesign grading around AI). The sentence is a grading rule, but what it forbids is submitting AI-generated work, which is the P19 rule almost word for word. A reader looking for 'do not submit AI-produced work' would look under P19. Final P19. Actor, phase, modality and unit_stance agreed.

units.why: The stated reason is that students must "be competent to surpass generative AI in the future - whether in academia, research, the workplace". Limiting AI for career readiness is P94.
units.anchor: competent to surpass generative AI in the future
units.fit_note: The goal is stated as being able to surpass AI in academia, research, the workplace or other domains, not careers alone.
units.resolution_why: Coder A coded P94 (careers as reason); coder B coded P41 (AI shortcuts the practice that builds skill). The passage says limiting AI is "necessary to ensure you are competent to surpass generative AI in the future - whether in academia, research, the workplace". It names careers among the domains and does not say AI shortcuts practice, so P94 fits better, partly. Final P94 with fit note.

units.why: The instructor will "produce, analyze, and provide AI-generated sample solutions" as a course baseline for students to surpass, a grading design built around AI (P35).
units.anchor: we will produce, analyze, and provide AI-generated sample solutions
units.resolution_why: Coder A coded phase before-course and unit_stance require; coder B during-work and neutral. "We will produce, analyze, and provide AI-generated sample solutions" is the instructor's course design, so before-course. It states how the course is built and does not require students to use AI, so unit_stance neutral. Type P35, actor instructor, modality informs agreed.

units.why: "AI contributions must be attributed" requires attribution of AI contributions, which is disclosure (P24).
units.anchor: AI contributions must be attributed
units.resolution_why: Found only by coder A, who put attribution and editing for accuracy in one P24 unit with a fit note. Two distinct rules, so split into two units: this attribution unit (P24) and the next unit for editing for accuracy (P31). Kept.

units.why: "edited for accuracy" requires students to correct AI contributions so they are accurate, which is verifying AI output (P31). It is the second rule in principle (2).
units.anchor: edited for accuracy
units.policy: AI contributions must be edited for accuracy.
units.resolution_why: Derived by the reconciler from coder A's attribution unit, whose fit note said it also requires editing for accuracy (P31). The source sentence has two rules joined by 'and', so they are separate units. Coder B covered accuracy only through 'facts must be true'.

units.why: "The use of AI resources must be open and documented" requires open disclosure (P24).
units.anchor: The use of AI resources must be open and documented
units.resolution_why: Found only by coder A. "The use of AI resources must be open and documented" is principle (3) of the three principles and requires open disclosure; real policy statement, P24 must. Kept.

units.why: "You are taking full responsibility for AI-generated materials as if you had produced them yourself" makes the student own all submitted AI-assisted work (P29).
units.anchor: You are taking full responsibility for AI-generated materials as if you had produced them yourself
units.resolution_why: Coder A coded unit_stance neutral; coder B permit. "You are taking full responsibility for AI-generated materials as if you had produced them yourself" assigns accountability and takes no position on whether AI may be used, so neutral. Type P29, actor, phase and modality agreed.

units.why: "facts must be true" requires students to check AI output for accuracy; P31.
units.anchor: facts must be true
units.policy: Facts in AI-generated material must be true.
units.fit_note: Short statement; does not say AI is often wrong.
units.resolution_why: Found only by coder B. "facts must be true" is a separate requirement in the sentence about taking responsibility (coder A did not code it). It requires students to ensure the accuracy of AI-generated content, so P31. Kept.

units.why: "A portion of your term grade will evaluate your documentation of AI use" requires keeping a record of AI use and grades it. Nearest type is P26; the grading of it is the extra.
units.anchor: A portion of your term grade will evaluate your documentation of AI use
units.fit_note: Part of the grade is based on the documentation, which the type does not mention.
units.resolution_why: Both coders coded P26, student, during-work, must, require; they only differed in fit note wording, which says that the grading of documentation is not part of the type. Merged.

units.why: "By keeping track of your AI use and sharing your experiences, we all gain understanding, identify potential issues" gives a collective-learning reason for documentation; closest is P55 (gathering evidence on AI's effect).
units.anchor: By keeping track of your AI use and sharing your experiences, we all gain understanding
units.fit_note: The documentation is for shared class learning, not formal evidence of learning effects.
units.resolution_why: Found only by coder A. "By keeping track of your AI use and sharing your experiences, we all gain understanding, identify potential issues" gives a reason for the documentation: collective learning about AI in a changing field. It is a real rationale statement; P55 is the nearest type, with the fit note that it is shared class learning. Kept.

units.why: "The use of generative AI is strictly prohibited in this course" is a blanket ban, so P01.
units.anchor: The use of generative AI is strictly prohibited in this course

units.why: "Closed Book Exam/Quiz The use of AI tools is not permitted" bars AI on exams and quizzes, so P22.
units.anchor: Closed Book Exam/Quiz The use of AI tools is not permitted

units.anchor: The use of generative AI tools is not permitted on writing assignments in this course
units.fit_note: The type is about treating prose differently; this unit is a prose-specific ban.

units.why: "By submitting a writing assignment, you attest that you are the only and original author" makes the student own and vouch for the submission (P29).
units.anchor: By submitting a writing assignment, you attest that you are the only and original author
units.resolution_why: Found only by coder A. "By submitting a writing assignment, you attest that you are the only and original author" is the writing-assignment version of the attestation (coder B coded only the code version). Real; P29, must. Kept.

units.why: "The use of generative AI tools to develop code is strictly prohibited" bans AI-produced code, so students may not have AI generate what they submit (P19).
units.anchor: The use of generative AI tools to develop code is strictly prohibited in this course

units.why: Attestation text "you attest that you are the only and original author of the code submitted" makes students own the submission, P29.
units.anchor: you attest that you are the only and original author of the code submitted
units.resolution_why: Found only by coder B. "you attest that you are the only and original author of the code submitted" is the code-assignment attestation (coder A coded the writing version only). Real; P29, must. Kept.

units.why: The samples "should be amended to reflect UNT and departmental policies as well as specifics of the classroom"; this tells instructors to adapt the templates. Closest is P110 (templates).
units.anchor: should be amended to reflect UNT and departmental policies
units.fit_note: It also says to align with UNT and departmental policies and the classroom. (Coder B: Says samples must fit university and department policy and the classroom.)
units.resolution_why: Coder A coded P110; coder B coded P04. The sentence says the sample statements "should be amended to reflect UNT and departmental policies as well as specifics of the classroom", an instruction on how to use templates, which is P110. Actor, phase and modality agreed.

documents.unit: Department of Computer Science and Engineering
documents.title: Academic Integrity (CSE)
documents.summary: The CSE department's integrity, misconduct and professionalism guidelines. A short AI section says unauthorized AI use is cheating under UNT Policy 6.003 and that AI cannot be used unless an instructor authorizes it, with fuller procedures promised later. The rest of the page sets department consequences for integrity violations and suggests a syllabus line.
documents.stance_why: The AI section states "Unless a professor or instructor gives explicit authorization, AI cannot be used to assist in the completion of assignments, projects, or papers." That bans AI by default and allows it only when an instructor explicitly permits it, which is restrict.

units.why: "The unauthorized use of any person or technology that assists in a student's assignment ... is considered cheating" classes unauthorized AI as cheating under policy 6.003 (P36).
units.anchor: use of any person or technology that assists in a student's assignment, project, or paper
units.policy: The unauthorized use of any person or technology that assists in a student's assignment, project, or paper is considered cheating under the UNT Student Academic Integrity Policy (UNT Policy 6.003).
units.resolution_why: Coder A coded phase when-misuse; coder B general. The sentence classifies unauthorized assistance as cheating, which is how misuse is categorized, the same phase used for the FAQ and library classification units. Type P36, actor student and modality informs agreed. Wording: normalized policy added because the anchor does not contain 'cheating'.

units.why: "Unless a professor or instructor gives explicit authorization, AI cannot be used" states what applies when there is no permission, which is the fallback rule (P06); it also is the department's default ban (P01), but the conditional "unless" form is the defining feature of P06.
units.anchor: Unless a professor or instructor gives explicit "authorization," AI cannot be used to assist

units.why: "Doing so will result in a 'cheating' violation" states the consequence of unauthorized AI use; the classification is P36, with no specific penalty.
units.anchor: Doing so will result in a "cheating" violation
units.resolution_why: Found only by coder B. "Doing so will result in a 'cheating' violation" states the consequence of unauthorized AI use in its own sentence; no specific penalty, so it is a classification (P36), not P37. Real; kept.

units.why: "If uncertain contact the instructor prior to using AI tools" tells students to ask before using AI (P10).
units.anchor: if uncertain contact the instructor prior to using AI tools

units.why: "A more complete procedures and guidelines will be made available soon" says the AI policy is incomplete and will be extended (P54).
units.anchor: A more complete procedures and guidelines will be made available soon
units.resolution_why: Coder A coded actor all; coder B admin. "A more complete procedures and guidelines will be made available soon" is the department saying it will issue guidance, so the department (admin) is the actor. Type P54, phase over-time and modality informs agreed.

units.why: The page lists penalties such as "Removal from the student's degree program" and denial of TA/IA/RA positions for integrity violations, which include unauthorized AI. This states concrete penalties in advance (P37).
units.anchor: Removal from the student's degree program
units.frag_end: documented warnings can escalate to these more serious consequences.
units.policy: Potential consequences of academic integrity violations include removal from the degree program, denial of future TA/IA/RA positions, denial of awards and recognition, termination of a TA/IA/RA position, impact on MS or PhD admissions, and removal of scholarship support; severe or repeated violations after documented warnings can escalate.
units.fit_note: The penalties are for all integrity and conduct violations, not AI specifically. (Coder B: General integrity consequences, not written for AI specifically.)

units.why: "Two reported and verified academic integrity violations in two separate courses" can lead to removal from the programs, a stated escalation threshold (P37).
units.anchor: Two reported and verified academic integrity violations in two separate courses with two separate instructors
units.fit_note: Applies to all integrity violations, not AI specifically. (Coder B: General integrity penalty; AI is a cheating violation under this page.)

units.why: TAs or IAs who facilitate violations face "Immediate expulsion"; this binds staff and sets a penalty, P37.
units.anchor: Immediate expulsion – verified assisting other students in cheating
units.fit_note: Binds TAs and IAs and is not AI-specific. The consequences are listed with 'not limited to'.
units.resolution_why: Found only by coder B. TAs or IAs who facilitate violations face "Immediate expulsion" among the consequences. It states a concrete penalty in advance (P37) for staff; coder B coded must-not, but the sentence lists consequences and does not itself command, so informs. Real; kept.

units.why: "Examinations are to involve no talking, no sharing/discussing, notes, or internet use unless authorized" sets closed-resource exam rules that exclude AI, so P22.
units.anchor: Examinations are to involve no talking, no sharing/discussing, notes, or internet use unless authorized
units.fit_note: AI is not named; internet use bars it indirectly. (Coder B: AI is not mentioned; rule is no internet or notes on exams.)
units.resolution_why: Coder A coded unit_stance restrict; coder B prohibit. "no talking, no sharing/discussing, notes, or internet use unless authorized" bans these except when authorized, which is restrict. Type P22, actor, phase and modality agreed.

units.why: "Violations will result in an automatic F in the course" fixes the penalty for exam cheating in advance (P37).
units.anchor: Violations will result in an automatic F in the course

units.why: "It is the student's responsibility to be aware of these policies. Lack of awareness is not grounds for appeal" puts the duty to know the rules on students (P78).
units.anchor: It is the student's responsibility to be aware of these policies

units.why: The department's actions are "intended to be corrective, educationally sound, fundamentally fair", which prefers an educative response over punishment (P68).
units.anchor: the Department's actions are intended to be corrective, educationally sound, fundamentally fair
units.fit_note: The sentence also says actions are fair and evidence-based. (Coder B: Also says actions rest on reliable evidence (P69); not AI-specific.)

units.why: Actions are "based on reliable evidence", a standard for findings of dishonesty (P69).
units.anchor: based on reliable evidence
units.fit_note: The standard is stated generally, without saying what counts as reliable.
units.resolution_why: Found only by coder A as its own unit (coder B folded it into its P68 unit with a fit note). "based on reliable evidence" is an evidence standard (P69) distinct from the educative-response rule, so it is kept as a separate unit.

units.why: The department "embraces the core values of trust and honesty" as the basis for integrity rules, a fairness and honesty rationale (P95).
units.anchor: promotes the integrity of learning and embraces the core values of trust and honesty
units.frag_end: core values of trust and honesty.
units.resolution_why: Found only by coder A. "promotes the integrity of learning and embraces the core values of trust and honesty" is the department's rationale for its rules, a real statement (P95). Kept.

units.why: "It is critical to reach out to instructors ... to clarify what constitutes an academic integrity violation when uncertain" tells students to ask when unsure (P10).
units.anchor: reach out to instructors, or relevant faculty and staff, to clarify what constitutes
units.fit_note: General integrity, not AI-specific.

units.why: "The academic integrity appeals process is available" to students who are reported, giving them a route to respond (P64).
units.anchor: If you are reported for academic integrity violations, the academic integrity appeals process is available

units.why: Instructors are told "In Syllabi we suggest you insert" a line applying the department integrity policies, which is sample syllabus language (P110) that also points syllabi to the AI rules.
units.anchor: In Syllabi we suggest you insert
units.policy: Instructors are suggested to insert in the syllabus a statement that all department policies on academic integrity and student conduct apply and giving the link to this page.
units.fit_note: The suggested wording points to department integrity policy and does not state AI rules.
units.resolution_why: Coder A coded P110 (course-start); coder B coded P09 (before-course). The passage says "In Syllabi we suggest you insert" a line, which supplies suggested syllabus wording (P110). It does not require an AI statement, and the suggested wording is not about AI, so P09 fits less well. Phase course-start because the line is put in the syllabus for students. Actor instructor and modality should agreed.

units.why: "Note all deviations from the department guidelines in the syllabus explicitly" lets instructors differ from the department rule if they say so in the syllabus. The point is who may set the rule (the instructor, as an exception), so P04; it is not a requirement to state an AI policy in every syllabus (P09).
units.anchor: Note all deviations from the department guidelines in the syllabus explicitly
units.fit_note: Instructor exceptions are allowed but must be written out in the syllabus; only deviations must be stated, not every AI expectation.
units.resolution_why: Coder A coded P09; coder B coded P04. P09 requires an AI statement in every syllabus; this sentence asks only for deviations from the department rule to be noted, and implies instructors may deviate. That is the instructor-sets-the-rule idea, so P04. Actor instructor, phase course-start and modality should agreed.
